quick.summary: How to guide audience attention by highlighting only the main point.
quick.takeaway: Highlight the one line that matters most. Make the rest soft gray.

beats.line: Five lines on my chart. Nobody knows where to look. Any ideas?
If it points to ten cities in the same color, you crash.
So my chart is causing a mental car crash.
Yes. Your audience suffers from high cognitive load.
Can I just say it is too cluttered?
You can. We need to guide their eyes.
Pick the one line that matters most. Make it bright.
And what about the other four lines?
Paint them soft gray. They become background context.
I highlight the hero, and whisper the rest.

quiz.question: What is the best way to fix a line chart that has too many bright colors?
options: Make the most important line bright, and the rest gray.
Use thicker lines for every category.
Remove the labels so there is less text to read.
Turn it into a pie chart with identical slices.
quiz.explanation: Graying out the background context makes the single most important message stand out immediately.

quiz.question: If you want an audience to understand a chart quickly, give every line a unique, bright color.
quiz.explanation: Too many bright colors create clutter. It is better to use color sparingly to guide attention.
